[Problem]{.card-kicker} **Longest Consecutive Sequence** [LC 128 · Longest Consecutive Sequence](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-consecutive-sequence/){difficulty="Medium"}

"Consecutive" is a statement about *values*, so sorting feels inevitable — but the required $O(n)$ forbids it, and a hash set gives the better primitive: with $s = \text{set}(a)$ you can ask "does $x-1$ exist?" instantly. Only **run starts** matter — values $x$ with no $x-1$ in $s$. Every value belongs to exactly one run and is stepped over by exactly one walk, the one that starts at the bottom of its run, so all the walks together take $O(n)$ steps even though a single walk can be long (@fig-hash-anim-runs).

[Solved in full in @sec-hash-p5-a.]{.card-link}

:::
